players.note: Dak Prescott has been on fire as the QB4 in fantasy points per game. Among 31 qualifying quarterbacks, Prescott is 13th in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, 16th in highly accurate throw rate, and eighth in hero throw rate. Prescott should have another strong QB1 showing this week. The Eagles pass defense isn't much to fear. Over their last five games, they have allowed the 11th-most EPA per dropback, the 12th-most fantasy points per dropback, and the 11th-highest passer rating. During that stretch, they have also managed to have the fourth-lowest pressure rate.

Deshaun Watson could be a QB1 this week. Among 32 qualifying passers, he is 13th in yards per attempt and passing success rate, 19th in catchable target rate, and 22nd in hero throw rate. The Raiders' pass defense has been bleeding out production to passing attacks all year. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fourth-most yards per attempt, the third-highest passing touchdown rate, the fourth-highest passing success rate, and the sixth-most fantasy points per dropback.

Kirk Cousins is the QB13 in fantasy points per game. Over the last two weeks as a Viking, he has been the QB14 and QB22 in weekly scoring. Among 32 qualifying passers, Cousins is 15th in yards per attempt, eighth in passing success rate, 25th in catchable target rate, and 18th in hero throw rate. Cousins should have a nice bounceback game this week. Over their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the sixth-most yards per attempt, the fifth-highest passing touchdown rate, the sixth-highest passing success rate, and the eighth-most fantasy points per dropback.

Tyler Shough is the QB14 in fantasy points per game. Among 32 qualifying passers, he is 25th in yards per attempt, 15th in passing success rate, 11th in catchable target rate, and 12th in hero throw rate. Shough has displayed some rushing production, which has helped raise his weekly ceiling and floor. Across his last five games, he has had at least 25 rushing yards four times. His passing production has been lackluster, with less than 250 passing yards in three of his last five games and zero multiple passing touchdown games since Week 6. Shough could flirt with QB1 production this week, but he's better viewed as a mid-range QB2. Cincy's pass defense has improved. Over their last five games, they have allowed the eighth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 13th-lowest passing success rate, and the third-lowest CPOE.

Joe Milton could have his fantasy showing of the season this week. Yes, that's not saying much, though. Over his last games, Milton has averaged only 10.25 fantasy points (QB31 in fantasy points per game) with zero passing touchdowns (zero interceptions). The rushing that propped up his stat line against the Giants fell off against the Steelers as he ran only five times for seven yards, so I wouldn't count on that this week. Milton has completed only 52.7% of his passes while averaging 155 passing yards. Milton has been horrible as a passer. Among 42 qualifying passers, he is 37th in yards per attempt, 41st in passing success rate, 39th in highly accurate throw rate, and 42nd in catchable target rate. Over their last five games, Dallas has remained a terrible pass defense, allowing the tenth-highest yards per attempt, the ninth-highest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-highest passing success rate, and the eighth-highest CPOE.

Over the last two weeks as Baltimore's starting quarterback, Jacoby Brissett has been the QB20 and QB17 in weekly fantasy scoring. Since Week 10, among 31 qualifying quarterbacks, Brissett is 15th in yards per attempt and highly accurate throw rate, 19th in passing success rate, seventh in catchable target rate, and 17th in hero throw rate. Brissett should be able to post decent QB2 numbers this week against a Texans' pass defense that might have turned a corner. Over their last five games, Houston has allowed the seventh-lowest passing success rate, the ninth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the fifth-lowest CPOE. Brissett should have volume on his side, though. With Brissett, Baltimore has leaned into the passing game with the third-highest passing rate.

The last time Bryce Young faced this pass defense, he was the QB24 for the week. Young completed 51.9% of his passes in that game with 163 passing yards (6.0 yards per attempt) and one passing touchdown (two picks). That game started Young's fall from grace and the weekly rollercoaster ride again. After that game, he has finished as the QB19, QB6, QB26, and QB11 in weekly scoring. Since Week 7, among 30 qualifying passers, Young has been 22nd in yards per attempt, 19th in passing success rate, 20th in catchable target rate, and 25th in hero throw rate. I expect Young to struggle again this week. Over their last five games, Tampa Bay has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per attempt, the 14th-lowest passing success rate, the second-fewest EPA per dropback, and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

Since Sean Payton took over play-calling duties, Bo Nix has been the QB23 in fantasy points per game. Among 32 qualifying quarterbacks since Week 5, Nix has ranked 28th in yards per attempt, 20th in aDOT and hero throw rate, 32nd in passing success rate, and tenth in deep ball rate. He still hasn't been a good quarterback despite Payton ramping up the motion rate (13th-best) and the play-action usage (eighth-best). I don't expect a standout performance this week from Nix, but Pittsburgh has been a middle-of-the-pack pass defense, so he could provide decent QB2 production. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the tenth-highest passing success rate while ranking 15th in yards per attempt, 17th in EPA per dropback, and 16th in CPOE.

After two starts, Fernando Mendoza looks like the real deal. Last week, he was the QB3 in fantasy scoring. In his previous start, against one of the best pass defenses in the NFL, he was the QB18 for the week. Mendoza is adding something with his legs weekly, with 22 rushing yards in both games and a rushing score. Last week, among 26 qualifying quarterbacks, Mendoza was 12th in yards per attempt, 22nd in catchable target rate, and 21st in highly accurate throw rate. Mendoza will have another tough test this week. He should post at least decent QB2 production. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per attempt and passing touchdown rate, the fifth-lowest passing success rate, and the fifth-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

Last week was Baker Mayfield's first game of the season with multiple passing touchdowns as the QB11 for the week. Over their last two weeks, among 24 qualifying passers, he has been 20th in yards per attempt, tenth in passing success rate, 23rd in aDOT, 17th in catchable target rate, and 16th in hero throw rate. Mayfield could have a decent QB2 stat line this week, but I'm not expecting more than that despite a good matchup this week. Over their last five games, Carolina has allowed the 13th-highest passing touchdown rate, the ninth-highest passing success rate, the second-highest CPOE, and the ninth-highest EPA per dropback.

Last week, Cam Ward stacked his third consecutive QB1 outing in a row as the QB5 for the week. Ward continues to get by with the Daniel Jones diet of quarterback play, with the Titans also going pace up and utilizing no-huddle heavily. Last week, the Titans led the NFL in no-huddle plays run. Since Week 8, among 27 qualifying passers, Ward has been 15th in yards per attempt, 11th in passing success rate, and first in RPO rate, with the second-lowest aDOT and the 11th-highest % of passing yardage coming from yards after the catch. Ward is just a run-of-the-mill QB2 this week. Across their last five games, the Jags have allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt, the fourth-lowest passer rating, the third-lowest passing success rate, and the fourth-lowest EPA per dropback.

The last time that Geno Smith faced this Miami secondary, he chucked it for 289 through the air with 9.3 yards per attempt and three passing scores. Smith was the QB5 for the week with 24.6 fantasy points. Smith could easily be a QB1 this week. Smith has been playing good football this season. Among 32 qualifying passers, Smith is tenth in yards per attempt, 12th in passing success rate, tenth in catchable target rate, and eighth in hero throw rate. Over their last five games, Miami has allowed the 12th-highest yards per attempt while allowing the 15th-highest passing success rate and CPOE.

Anthony Richardson will be the Colts' starting quarterback moving forward. He has attempted only four passes this season, so there's nothing to take away from that. 2025 was essentially a lost season for him as well. We have to go all the way back to 2024. In that season, he averaged 7.8 rushing attempts and 45.4 rushing yards per game. Richardson had only three weeks with QB1 finishes in weekly scoring. In 2024, among 44 qualifying passers, Richardson was dead last in passing success rate, highly accurate throw rate, and catchable target rate. I'm not expecting Richardson to be an amazing passer, but if he can add some production with his legs weekly, he could at least be a serviceable QB2. Richardson will have a long day at the office in Week 12. The Giants' pass defense has been no joke. Over their last five games, they have allowed the fifth-fewest yards per attempt, the second-lowest passing success rate, and the seventh-lowest EPA per dropback. During this stretch, they also have the seventh-best pressure rate and the sixth-best quick pressure rate.

Sam Darnold will be back under center this week. Darnold is the QB24 in fantasy points per game this season, with only two games with more than 16 fantasy points. Among 32 qualifying quarterbacks, Darnold is 20th in yards per attempt, 22nd in passing success rate, eighth in catchable target rate, 21st in hero throw rate, and he has the fourth-highest turnover-worthy throw rate. Darnold should be able to scrape together a decent QB2 stat line this week. The 49ers' pass defense hasn't been an elite unit. Over their last five games, San Francisco has allowed the 11th-highest passing touchdown rate, the 14th-highest passing success rate, the 11th-highest CPOE, and ranked 18th in EPA per dropback.

I feel bad for Michael Penix. A ticked-off Minnesota pass defense is likely to light him up this week like a Christmas tree. Penix is the QB24 in fantasy points per game. Among 32 qualifying passers, Penix is 18th in yards per attempt, 21st in passing success rate, 27th in CPOE, and 29th in catchable target rate. Over their last six games, Minnesota has allowed the 12th-lowest passing touchdown rate and passer rating, the eighth-lowest EPA per dropback, and the fifth-fewest fantasy points per dropback. Also in that span, Minnesota has had the highest pressure rate.

Tommy DeVito looked horrible against the Lions in relief of Drake Maye. He completed only 50% of his 24 passes with 3.4 yards per attempt, 81 passing yards, and a 1:1 touchdown-to-interception ratio. To find previous starting experience recently, we have to go back to 2024, when DeVito had two starts. In those two starts, he was the QB24 and QB32 in weekly scoring. He didn't manage even 200 passing yards or 6.2 yards per attempt in either outing. In 2024, DeVito had only a 5.68 aDOT and a 52.3% highly accurate throw rate, so I don't have a ton of faith in DeVito to perform well in Week 12. The matchup is nice for DeVito, so maybe he does flash a fantasy pulse this week. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the eighth-most yards per attempt, the tenth-highest passing touchdown rate, the fifth-highest passing success rate, and the eighth-most EPA per dropback.

The Cardinals are starting Josh Johnson again this week. Last week, he was the QB22 in weekly scoring with five rushing yards, a 58.1% completion rate, 155 passing yards, and one passing score. Johnson had only 5.0 yards per attempt, a 38.7% passing success rate, and a 48.4% highly accurate throw rate. It wasn't great, Bob. Johnson is better left on the bench this week. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-fewest fantasy points per dropback, and ranked 16th in passer rating allowed.

In his two starts, Kyle McCord has finished as the QB21 and QB27 in weekly scoring. The wheels fell off last week as he completed only 36.4% of his passes with 102 scoreless passing yards (one interception). Overall, he has been abysmal as a passer with only a 35.4% highly accurate throw rate, a 26.2% off-target rate, a 32.3% passing success rate, and 4.78 yards per attempt. McCord could get benched at any point for Brady Cook. I can't trust him in any format.
